title: Compounding $1 at 100% for one year
sub: More frequent payments, smaller each time. The total approaches e, not infinity.

frames.caption: Bernoulli's question: a bank pays 100% interest a year on $1. How much do you have after a year if the interest is paid once? Twice, at half the rate each time? Every day?
Paid once a year: each payment adds 1/1 of the balance. The steps get smaller but more frequent. After a year: $2.00000.
Paid twice a year: each payment adds 1/2 of the balance. The steps get smaller but more frequent. After a year: $2.25000.
Paid quarterly: each payment adds 1/4 of the balance. The steps get smaller but more frequent. After a year: $2.44141. More payments help, but less and less.
Paid monthly: each payment adds 1/12 of the balance. The steps get smaller but more frequent. After a year: $2.61304. More payments help, but less and less.
Paid daily: each payment adds 1/365 of the balance. The steps get smaller but more frequent. After a year: $2.71457. More payments help, but less and less.
In the limit of compounding continuously, the staircase becomes the smooth curve eᵗ (aqua), and the year ends at e = 2.71828…, not infinity. Daily compounding is already within 0.005 of it.
